Issues.Title: perf(forms): avoid retaining AbstractControl in signal forms
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [x] Other... Please describe: Performance / bundle size optimization

## What is the current behavior?

`FieldNodeContext.valueOf` checks `result instanceof AbstractControl` to throw `NG1907` when reading an `AbstractControl` inside a regular `form()`. That value reference prevents `AbstractControl` (along with control event classes and validator helpers) from being tree-shaken in applications that only use signal forms.

Issue Number: Fixes #71621

## What is the new behavior?

- Introduces an internal symbol-based type guard `ɵisAbstractControl` that checks a private `Symbol` set in `AbstractControl`'s constructor without referencing the `AbstractControl` class value, remaining compatible with Closure Compiler (`jscompiler`) property renaming and ES2022 class tree-shaking.
- Adds a bundling symbol test (`//packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals:symbol_test`) verifying that `AbstractControl` and its associated classes/helpers are tree-shaken in signal forms bundles.

### Impact / Dropped Symbols

- **In `[formField]` apps (`//packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals`):** Drops **19 symbols** (~1.9 KB gzipped) from `@angular/forms`:
  - Core model & statuses: `AbstractControl`, `VALID`, `INVALID`, `PENDING`, `DISABLED`
  - Control event classes: `ValueChangeEvent`, `StatusChangeEvent`, `PristineChangeEvent`, `TouchedChangeEvent`, `FormSubmittedEvent`
  - Validator & options helpers: `addValidators`, `removeValidators`, `hasValidator`, `makeValidatorsArray`, `coerceToValidator`, `coerceToAsyncValidator`, `pickValidators`, `pickAsyncValidators`, `isOptionsObj`
- **In model-only `form()` apps (without `[formField]`):** Drops **~75 symbols** (~4.7 KB gzipped), additionally tree-shaking `Validators`, all built-in validator functions, `ControlEvent`, `FormResetEvent`, RxJS async validator helpers (`forkJoin`, `from`, `innerFrom`, `scheduled`, `map`, etc.), and `tslib` async generator helpers.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

### Follow-up opportunity for `[formField]`
`FormField` still retains `NgControl`, `AbstractControlDirective`, `Validators`, `RequiredValidator`, `FormResetEvent`, and `ReactiveValidationError` because:
1. `FormField` provides `{provide: NgControl, useFactory: () => inject(FormField).interopNgControl}` for CVA / `inject(NgControl)` interop, and `NgControl` extends `AbstractControlDirective` and references `FormResetEvent`, `RequiredValidator`, and `ReactiveValidationError` in its methods.
2. `InteropNgControl.hasValidator` and `cvaControlCreate` reference `Validators.required` and `Validators.compose`.

Decoupling the `NgControl` DI token from its directive implementation and avoiding direct references to the `Validators` class in `InteropNgControl` / `cvaControlCreate` could drop an additional ~55 symbols (including the remaining RxJS `forkJoin` / `from` async validator helpers) from `[formField]` bundles in a follow-up.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): emit namespace imports for standalone declarations in remote scopes
Issues.Body:
When an `NgModule` imports or re-exports an in-program standalone declaration, ngtsc resolves its scope entry from the declaration's own metadata rather than the import identifier in the module file, so remote scoping emits it through a namespace import.

Previously the preprocessor kept the module file's local import alias on the reference, causing `ɵɵsetComponentScope` to emit the bare identifier instead. These changes strip the importer aliases for non-`.d.ts` standalone declarations in `NgModule` scopes to match ngtsc.

Also fixes some tests that weren't running against the preprocessor.

Issues.Title: fix(docs-infra): link directive selector aliases to the right API page
Issues.Body:
`extractAliasesFromSelector` collects every `[attr]` in a selector, including ones inside `:not(...)` and compound selectors, so `NgModel` and `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` both claim `ngModel`, `formControl` and `formControlName`. `mapManifestToEntries` writes aliases with no collision check, so the last claimant wins (`SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor`), and an alias can also delete a real entry, which is why `email()` never linked.

Aliases are now collected per name. When several directives claim one, the one named after it wins, otherwise it stays unlinked. An alias never replaces a real entry, and `email` joins the names that are not linked on their own (`required`, `min`, ...).

| Text | Links to today | Links to now | Links | Pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ngModel` | `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` | `NgModel` | 56 | 13 |
| `formControlName` | `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` | `FormControlName` | 23 | 6 |
| `formControl` | `SelectMultipleControlValueAccessor` | `FormControlDirective` | 11 | 3 |
| `routerLink` | `RouterLinkWithHref` | `RouterLink` | 63 | 12 |
| `formGroup`, `formArray` | `NgForm` | `FormGroupDirective`, `FormArrayDirective` | 13 | 5 |
| `formGroupName`, `formArrayName` | `NgControlStatusGroup` | `FormGroupName`, `FormArrayName` | 5 | 1 |
| `ngFor` | `NgForOf` | `NgFor` | 6 | 4 |
| `email()`, `required()`, ... | not linked | `forms/signals/*` | 61 | 12 |

https://angular.dev/guide/forms/form-validation#:~:text=actor%2Dform%2Dtemplate.component.html%20(name)
Hovering `[(ngModel)]` in the form-validation guide, before (angular.dev) and after (this branch):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18cae50f-3215-4812-8d1c-263254002cf7

Diffed every link in the generated guide HTML before and after: 178 wrong links removed, 238 added. Four aliases now render unlinked (`type`, `multiple`, `ngNoCva`, `ngNoForm`).

Issues.Title: perf(forms): avoid creating unused field injectors
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the guidelines.
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added.
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (not needed: no public API change).

## PR Type

- [x] Other: performance improvement

## What is the current behavior?

Fields create an injector as soon as they have any metadata, even when every key is plain metadata. Built-in rules such as `required()`, `min()`, and `debounce()` therefore allocate injectors they never use. Removing a field without an injector also creates one just to destroy it.

Fixes #71623.

## What is the new behavior?

Enter the field's injection context only for a managed key's `create` callback, and destroy only an existing field injector. Managed factories still run eagerly, in order, outside the reactive context, and share the same injector for a field.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

No public API or scheduling changes. Field removal still destroys managed metadata and cancels pending HTTP validation.

## Validation

- Signal Forms Node suite: **557 specs, 0 failures**.
- Signal Forms Chromium suite: **362 specs, 0 failures**.
- Two allocation regression tests fail on unmodified main.
- Added coverage for plain metadata reactivity, built-in rules, managed-key injection and shared contexts, exactly-once removal cleanup, and pending HTTP validator cancellation.
- `ng-dev format`, Prettier, and `git diff --check` pass.

### Production-build check

An order-entry page renders 1,000 rows, with a `required()` SKU input and a `min()` quantity input in each row. Both optimized builds use the same application and instrumentation; one has these two changes transplanted into Angular Forms 22.2.3 (CLI/build 22.2.4). Node 24.22.1, Chromium 158.0.8117.0, seven alternating baseline/patched pairs in fresh browser contexts.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Field injectors created while rendering 2,000 inputs | 2,000 | 0 |
| Injectors created while removing the rows | 1,000 | 0 |
| Median additional live JS heap after GC | 41,739,092 bytes | 40,794,800 bytes |

This saves about **0.90 MiB** of live JS heap in that fixture. These are post-GC JS heap deltas, not peak memory or process RSS.

Median create-to-stable time was 259.8 / 254.4 ms; removal-to-stable was 60.8 / 56.3 ms. Samples overlap, so the concrete result is the avoided allocation and memory reduction, not a general latency guarantee. A separate 50-row control also preserved input count, editing/model propagation, validation, and row removal in all seven pairs. No page errors occurred.

The benchmark counts `Injector.create` calls using identical instrumentation in both builds. The application checks input rendering, required validation, edit propagation and successful removal. The installed Forms bundle was restored after building. The benchmark/support files are outside this PR.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): report errors at arrow parameters
Issues.Body:
Fixes #71733

## Why the change

Under `strictTemplates`, a TypeScript error that starts at a template arrow function parameter, such as a callback that declares a parameter its caller never passes, is silently dropped; with this fix Angular reports it at the parameter.

## Special things to note

- This PR rewrites the existing spec `should ignore diagnostics on arrow function parameters`, which asserted the `D:ignore` marker. The marker's only purpose was hiding implicit `any` errors, and those stay hidden. See [Why the old `D:ignore` spec changes](#why-the-old-dignore-spec-changes).
- The fix depends on correct parameter locations. The parser left the expression's offset out of them, so inside `{{…}}` they started too early (`{(val` instead of `val`, and further off in later interpolations). This PR fixes that too. Event bindings have no offset, so they weren't affected.
- Newly reported errors also include duplicate parameter names: `(a, a) => a` now reports TS2300 at both `a`s. Language service: go-to-definition on an arrow parameter reference now returns the parameter (`val`) instead of the enclosing expression (`val + 1`).

## Change outline

The template from the issue:

```html
<button (click)="retry((attempt) => load(attempt))">Retry</button>
```

What the type-check block emits for the arrow function. Other location comments are left out:

```diff
- (this).retry(attempt /*D:ignore*/ => ...)
+ (this).retry(attempt /*24,31*/ => ...)
```

How the TS2345 error, which starts at `attempt`, is mapped back to the template:

```diff
 translateDiagnostic(TS2345 at `attempt`)
   shouldReportDiagnostic            → TS2345 isn't filtered by code
   findSourceLocation(`attempt`)
-    has the D:ignore marker         → null → error dropped
+    has a location comment          → reported at `attempt`
```

Parameter locations from the parser, for `{{a}} {{(foo, bar) => foo + bar}}`:

```diff
- foo → `{a}} {{(foo`    bar → `{{(foo, bar`
+ foo → `foo`            bar → `bar`
```

### Why the old `D:ignore` spec changes

`type_check_block_spec.ts` had `should ignore diagnostics on arrow function parameters`, which expected `(a /*D:ignore*/, b /*D:ignore*/) =>`. It came from 87a422358b (#66294), the commit that added template arrow functions. The commit message and the PR don't discuss the marker. The one stated reason is the code comment that commit put on it:

> Ignore diagnostics on the node to skip diagnostics from `noImplicitAny` since users aren't able to set types on the parameters. Note that this is preferable to setting their types to `any`, because it allows us to infer the types when the arrow function is passed as a callback.

Both goals still hold without the marker:

| What the marker protected | What protects it now | Spec, all passing before and after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| No implicit `any` error (TS7006) on parameters that templates can't annotate | `shouldReportDiagnostic` drops TS7006 everywhere in the type-check block. It has done so since 2019 (#33125), before arrow functions existed. Template arrow parameters can only be plain names, so TS7006 is the only implicit `any` error they can produce. | `should not report implicit any errors on arrow functions defined in @let` (existing, from the same commit, unchanged), `should not report implicit any errors on arrow functions without a contextual type` (new) |
| Parameter types are still inferred from the callback, not forced to `any` | Unchanged. Parameters are still emitted without a type; only the trailing comment differs. | `should infer the types of parameters of arrow functions passed in as callbacks` (existing, unchanged), `should not report errors on contextually typed arrow function parameters` (new) |
| (Not stated, but also hidden) Unused parameter errors (TS6133, TS6199) | `shouldReportDiagnostic` drops both codes. | `should not report unused arrow function parameters` (new, in `typecheck/test/diagnostics_spec.ts`, with `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters`) |

The marker also hid every other error that starts at a parameter, which is the bug this PR fixes. The rewritten spec, `should add span info to arrow function parameters`, now expects `(a /*3,4*/, b /*6,7*/) =>`.

Changed files:

```text
packages/compiler/src/
├── typecheck/expression.ts           # parameter gets a location comment, not D:ignore
└── expression_parser/parser.ts       # parameter location includes the expression offset
packages/compiler-cli/
├── test/ngtsc/template_typecheck_spec.ts               # 2 specs that fail before, 2 that must stay silent
├── src/ngtsc/typecheck/test/diagnostics_spec.ts        # duplicate names (fails before), unused parameters (stays silent)
└── src/ngtsc/typecheck/test/type_check_block_spec.ts   # expects location comments
packages/compiler/test/expression_parser/parser_spec.ts # parameter locations in a second {{…}}
packages/language-service/test/definitions_spec.ts      # expects `val` instead of `val + 1`
```

## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

A template type error is not reported when TypeScript places it at an arrow function parameter. Examples are a callback with more parameters than its caller passes, a callback that returns a function instead of a value, and duplicate parameter names.

Issue Number: #71733

## What is the new behavior?

The error is reported at the parameter. Implicit `any` and unused-parameter errors on template arrow functions are still not reported.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Apps that contain such an error will now fail to compile under `strictTemplates`. The error was always there, but Angular didn't report it.

## Other information

The duplicate-name and unused-parameter specs are in `typecheck/test/diagnostics_spec.ts` rather than the ngtsc suite. Under the preprocessor backend (`ngtsc_ngp`), the compiled component code is type-checked as well, and its copy of the arrow function produces its own `Duplicate identifier` and TS6133 errors without a template location. That happens with and without this PR. `diagnostics_spec.ts` checks only the type-check block, so these specs pass on both backends.

Template arrow functions were added in 21.2.0, so 22.2.x has this bug too. This is a candidate for the patch branch. #52322 is a precedent: it surfaced comparison errors that an ignore marker hid, landed as a plain fix, and was cherry-picked to the release branch.

Issues.Title: Template type checking drops errors that start at an arrow function parameter
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler, compiler-cli

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

With `strictTemplates`, Angular doesn't report a type error in a template arrow function when TypeScript places that error at one of the function's parameters. The template compiles, and the mistake reaches runtime.

A common case is a callback that declares a parameter the caller never passes:

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  template: `<button (click)="retry((attempt) => load(attempt))">Retry</button>`,
})
export class App {
  retry(fn: () => void) {
    fn();
  }
  load(attempt: number) {}
}
```

`retry` calls `fn` with no arguments, so `attempt` is always `undefined`. In a `.ts` file, TypeScript rejects this call:

```text
TS2345: Argument of type '(attempt: any) => void' is not assignable to parameter of type '() => void'.
  Target signature provides too few arguments. Expected 1 or more, but got 0.
```

In the template, Angular reports nothing. The same happens when a callback returns a function instead of a value, such as `count.update((v) => () => v + 1)`.

TypeScript places most callback errors elsewhere, so Angular still reports them. For example, `count.update((v) => String(v))` reports TS2322 at `String(v)`.

Expected: Angular reports the error at the parameter (`attempt`), the same way it reports any other template type error.

**Cause:** the type-check code marks every arrow function parameter with a "skip diagnostics" comment ([expression.ts#L386](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler/src/typecheck/expression.ts#L386)), so [`findSourceLocation`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/tcb_util.ts#L211) drops every error that starts there. The marker was meant to hide implicit `any` errors on parameters that templates can't annotate, but [`shouldReportDiagnostic`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/diagnostics.ts#L29) already filters those by error code.

**Fix:** the linked PR gives each parameter its source location instead of the marker. Inferred parameter types don't change. Implicit `any` and unused-parameter errors stay hidden.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

No hosted reproduction. The snippet in the description is self-contained: paste it into any Angular 21.2+ app with `strictTemplates` turned on. The linked PR adds regression tests.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
None. The template compiles without errors.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 21.2.0 and later, including 22.2.x and 22.3.0-next.2 (main at 5d929e57e4).
Reproduced with compiler-cli tests in packages/compiler-cli/test/ngtsc/template_typecheck_spec.ts.
```

### Anything else?

Template arrow functions were added in 21.2.0, and the marker has been there since.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): detect @angular/core compilations like ngtsc in the preprocessor
Issues.Body:
The preprocessor recognized `@angular/core` by walking up to the nearest `package.json` named `@angular/core`, which ngtsc never does and which a host without file system access cannot do. Follow ngtsc's rule instead: the internal `angularCoreCompilation` option, falling back to the tsconfig's `_isAngularCoreCompilation`, then to an explicit `r3SymbolsFile`, and otherwise to whether the root `r3_symbols.ts` exports `ITS_JUST_ANGULAR = true` (ngtsc's `isAngularCorePackage`).

The `ITS_JUST_ANGULAR` check reads `r3_symbols.ts` through the query engine, so edits to it invalidate dependent analyses. A new pseudo-dependency on the `r3_symbols.ts` root lookup re-runs only the queries that read it when the roots add or remove that file, instead of every query on each root change.

Also remove the unused `resolve_to_dts` helper.

Issues.Title: fix(platform-browser): remove test root elements whose id was replaced by a host binding
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`DOMTestComponentRenderer` removes the root elements of earlier tests with `querySelectorAll('[id^=root]')`. When the root component sets or removes its own `id` (`host: {'[attr.id]': ...}`, `[id]`, `@HostBinding('attr.id')`), the `root<N>` id is gone, so the element is never removed. It stays in `document.body` for the rest of the run, and every later test that creates the component adds another one.

Issue Number: #35215

## What is the new behavior?

The renderer also keeps a reference to the root element it inserted last and removes it at the same points as the elements matched by id (module teardown, and the next `insertRootElement`). One reference is enough because `insertRootElement` already removes the previous root elements before it adds a new one.

The `root<N>` id and the `#root<N>` selector that TestBed passes to `ComponentFactory.create` are unchanged, so custom `TestComponentRenderer` implementations are not affected. Changing that selector is what held back #59711 (failures with custom renderers, per the comments there). Those custom renderers also keep their current behaviour for this bug.

The reference lives outside the class because every testing module gets its own renderer instance: with `destroyAfterEach: false`, the element of one test is removed by the next test's renderer.

Because the element is now removed by reference, two cases change besides the host binding one:

- it is also removed when the component removed its id, when the test moved it out of the document (for example into a detached container or a shadow root), or when a later test provides a different `DOCUMENT`;
- if a test creates a second component, the first root element is detached even when its id was replaced. Root elements that keep their id are already detached in that case today.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

- New tests in `packages/core/test/test_bed_spec.ts` cover module teardown enabled and disabled.
- I could not run the Bazel targets locally. I ran the two new tests and the rest of the `TestBed module teardown` block against the published 22.2.3 packages in JIT mode with Jasmine, with the same change applied to `@angular/platform-browser/fesm2022/testing.mjs`. I used two environments with zoneless change detection: `BrowserTestingModule` with jsdom, and `ServerTestingModule` with domino as in `tools/testing/node_tests.init.mts`. Neither loads zone.js, and the browser one has no `NoopAnimationsModule`. In both, the two new tests fail without the change and pass with it, and the other tests pass in both cases.
- The same problem was reported downstream in testing-library/angular-testing-library#398.
- Not changed here: the `[id^=root]` query also removes the user's own elements whose id starts with `root` (for example `#rootMenu`) when a component is created and at module teardown. Should that be narrowed in this PR, or in a separate issue?

Fixes #35215
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(platform-browser): remove test root elements whose id was replaced by a host binding" (#71724)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): add a TODO for spy strategies configured with withArgs in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
Spy strategies configured for specific arguments, such as `spyOn(service, 'calc').withArgs(1).and.returnValue(2)`, were converted to `vi.spyOn(service, 'calc').mockReturnValue(undefined).withArgs(1).mockReturnValue(2)` without a TODO comment. Vitest mocks have no `withArgs` method, so the migrated test failed with a TypeError.

Add a TODO comment for these strategies instead, since they need to be migrated manually, for example with `mockImplementation()`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@schematics/angular): add a TODO for spy strategies configured with withArgs in refactor-jasmine-vitest" (#34620)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): add a TODO for negated expectAsync matchers in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
Negated async matchers such as `expectAsync(promise).not.toBeResolved()` were left unchanged without a TODO comment, so the migrated test failed at runtime because `expectAsync` does not exist in Vitest.

Negated async matchers have no exact Vitest equivalent, so add the existing unsupported `expectAsync` matcher TODO comment to them.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): explain the latest version fallback when ng add finds no compatible version
Issues.Body:
When no version of the package satisfies the peer dependencies of the project, `ng add` reports `Unable to find compatible package.` and then continues to install the version of the `latest` tag. The explanation that the `latest` tag is used was dropped when the command was migrated to the new package manager abstraction, so the installation that follows the message is unexpected.

Restore the `Using 'latest' tag.` explanation.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): explain the latest version fallback when ng add finds no compatible version" (#34615)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): ignore registry manifests that do not match the requested version
Issues.Body:
Modern yarn returns the manifest of the latest version instead of an error when the requested version or range does not exist (for example, `yarn npm info @angular/core@99.99.99` prints the latest version with exit code 0). As a result, `ng add` and `ng update` could continue with an unrelated version instead of reporting that the requested version does not exist.

Return `null` from `getRegistryManifest` when the fetched version does not satisfy the requested version or range.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): ignore registry manifests that do not match the requested version" (#34617)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): keep the meaning of negated toHaveBeenCalledOnceWith in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
`expect(spy).not.toHaveBeenCalledOnceWith(...)` was split into `not.toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` and `not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)`, which asserts that neither condition holds instead of not both. For example, a spy called twice with the same arguments passed before the migration and failed after it.

Transform the negated form to `not.toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(...)`, which has the same meaning.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@schematics/angular): keep the meaning of negated toHaveBeenCalledOnceWith in refactor-jasmine-vitest" (#34616)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): strip terminal escape sequences in modern yarn error parser
Issues.Body:
Modern Yarn formats error detail fields such as `Response Code` with ANSI color sequences and OSC 8 hyperlinks before passing them to `StreamReport`, which serializes the formatted strings verbatim into its JSON line output. When colors are enabled, such as by default on GitHub Actions even over non-TTY pipes or via `FORCE_COLOR` and `.yarnrc.yml` settings, escape codes appear around both the `Response Code` label and status number. As a result, `parseYarnModernError` failed to match the HTTP status code, fell back to the generic `YN0035` code instead of `E404` for missing packages, and leaked raw control sequences into the parsed summary and detail text.

Strip VT control characters from modern Yarn error messages prior to matching an anchored `Response Code` line, and ignore 2xx status codes for consistency with the Yarn Classic parser. In addition, split multi-line error payloads such as `YN0001` exception stack traces so `summary` only retains the first line while remaining lines move into `detail`, fall back to `UNKNOWN_ERROR` when `displayName` is an empty string (when `enableMessageNames` is disabled), and return `null` directly when no JSON error lines are present instead of delegating to `parseNpmLikeError` on every successful command output.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): strip terminal escape sequences in modern yarn error parser" (#34614)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): keep the default ng-packagr output path in use-library-builder
Issues.Body:
The migration only sets `outputPath` when the ng-packagr configuration has a `dest`. Without it, ng-packagr writes to `dist` within the package directory, while the library builder defaults to `dist/<project>`, so the migrated library is silently built to a different location.

Set `outputPath` to the ng-packagr default when `dest` is not set. A new spec fails without this change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@schematics/angular): keep the default ng-packagr output path in use-library-builder" (#34603)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): handle modern yarn registry error output and 404 detection
Issues.Body:
Modern yarn (v2+) reports registry errors as JSON lines on `stdout`, one per message line, such as `{"type":"error","displayName":"YN0035","data":"Package not found"}` followed by a `Response Code: 404 (Not Found)` line. Because `parseNpmLikeError` did not recognize this format, querying a package that does not exist under modern yarn threw the original `Process exited with code 1.` error instead of returning `null`.

Add a `parseYarnModernError` parser for the modern yarn descriptor that reads these JSON lines and returns the HTTP status as the error code, so not-found responses are normalized to `E404`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): handle modern yarn registry error output and 404 detection" (#34606)

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #25705

Running `ng generate m help` (and similar) shows the CLI help menu instead of running the schematic with a positional argument named `help`.

The initial argv parse treated any bare token `help` as the global help flag.

## What is the new behavior?

Help is detected only from explicit `--help`, `-h`, or `--json-help`. Positionals named `help` are passed through to schematics (e.g. `ng generate m help` generates a module named `help`).

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): allow command arguments named `help`
Issues.Body:
Previously, `localYargs.help('help', ...)` was always enabled regardless of whether `--help` was passed. In Yargs, enabling `.help()` also registers an implicit `help` command/positional trigger, causing commands with a positional argument named `help` (such as `ng generate component help`) to display the CLI help output instead of executing the command.

Only enable Yargs help handling when `--help` is present in the parsed options.

Fixes #25705
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): allow command arguments named `help`" (#34609)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): resolve schematic working directory from project root
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #21660

In a multi-project workspace, `ng generate` from a project root (e.g. `projects/app1`) uses the workspace-relative working directory as the schematic `path` default. Files are created under the project folder instead of `src/app` / `src/lib`.

## What is the new behavior?

The `workingDirectory` smart default is resolved relative to the active project root. From the project root, schematics receive no working-directory override and apply their usual default path (`src/app` or `src/lib`). From deeper folders inside the project, paths remain relative to the project tree.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Fixes angular/angular-cli#21660

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): accept the project as a positional argument in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #34387, where @alan-agius4 noted that the schematic should accept the positional argument.

The karma-to-vitest migration suggests running ng g @schematics/angular:refactor-jasmine-vitest <project_name>, but the schematic only accepts the project through the --project option, so the suggested command fails with Unknown argument.

Read the project from the first positional argument. When it is not provided, the schematic still uses the only project of the workspace.

Note: an option can only have one $default, so the project is no longer inferred from the current directory ($source: projectName). In a multi-project workspace, running the schematic without a project name now reports the available projects instead. If keeping that inference is preferred, it could be done with a hidden workingDirectory option as suggested by the bot. Happy to add it.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@schematics/angular): accept the project as a positional argument in refactor-jasmine-vitest" (#34605)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): support array options defined in oneOf schemas
Issues.Body:
Previously, `getSupportedTypes` in `json-schema.ts` only checked top-level `items` when determining if an `array` type in a JSON schema was supported on the CLI. Options like `allowedHosts` in `@angular/build:dev-server`, which define their `array` schema inside a `oneOf` alongside `boolean`, had their `array` type filtered out and were registered in Yargs as `boolean` only.

Additionally, when an option supports both `array` (or `string`) and `boolean`, Yargs parses bare flags (e.g. `--allowed-hosts`) as `[]` and `--allowed-hosts=true` as `['true']`. This change checks `oneOf`/`anyOf` subschemas for supported array items and coerces empty or boolean-like values to booleans when `boolean` is also a supported type.

Fixes #33955
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): support array options defined in oneOf schemas" (#34607)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): skip other projects when finding secondary entry points in use-library-builder
Issues.Body:
The migration discovers secondary entry points by walking the library's root directory. For a library at the workspace root, this includes the directories of the other projects, so their ng-packagr configurations are added to the root library's `exports` and deleted before those libraries are migrated.

Skip the root directories of other workspace projects while discovering secondary entry points. A new spec fails without this change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@schematics/angular): skip other projects when finding secondary entry points in use-library-builder" (#34604)

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

Pattern from Angular testing guide

```ts
let heroServiceSpy: jasmine.SpyObj<HeroService>;

beforeEach(() => {
  heroServiceSpy = jasmine.createSpyObj('HeroService', ['getHeroes']);
});
```

is migrated to `MockedObject<HeroService>` variable and object literal with only `getHeroes`. Jasmine `createSpyObj` returns `any` so it compiled before, after migration `tsc` fails with

```
error TS2322: Type '{ getHeroes: Mock<Procedure>; }' is not assignable to type 'MockedObject<HeroService>'.
```

File is reported as transformed and there is no TODO

## What is the new behavior?

When `createSpyObj` initializes or is assigned to variable annotated with `jasmine.SpyObj<T>`, literal is cast `as MockedObject<T>` and type import is added. Declaration is looked up in nearest enclosing block, so `svc` declared in two `describe` blocks gets its own type in each. Migrated spec from above passes `tsc --strict` (TS 6.0, vitest 5.0)

New spec cases cover assignment, initializer and two describe blocks with same name, they fail on main

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Cast types members that were not spied as present, same as `jasmine.SpyObj<T>` with untyped `createSpyObj` did before migration. Other option is TODO without cast, I went with cast since it keeps migrated tests compiling

Issues.Title: fix(@ngtools/webpack): elide non-value aliases and remaining type-only AST constructs
Issues.Body:
Follow up to https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/34582 to cover remaining pure-type import elision cases and
partial specifier removal in `replaceBootstrap`:

- Elide imported alias symbols that do not resolve to a runtime value (or
  traverse a type-only alias declaration), handling non-`type` interface
  re-exports (`export { Foo }`) and interface parameter types under
  `emitDecoratorMetadata`.
- Only rewrite a partially elided import declaration when a runtime value
  import must be removed or when the declaration was already replaced by a
  previous transformer. TypeScript skips its own import elision for
  declarations replaced by a transformer, so leaving other declarations
  untouched avoids retaining specifiers that TypeScript would have otherwise
  elided (such as inlined `const enum` imports).
- Skip all non-`ExpressionWithTypeArguments` `TypeNode`s when
  `emitDecoratorMetadata` is disabled, and unconditionally skip
  `TypeQueryNode` (`typeof X`), `ImportTypeNode`,
  `IndexSignatureDeclaration`, ambient `declare` statements, and external
  `export ... from '...'` declarations.
- Recursively visit child AST nodes when applying `elideImports` removals in
  `replaceBootstrap` so individual `ImportSpecifier`s are removed when
  `platformBrowserDynamic` shares an import with other used runtime exports.

Issues.Title: fix(material/slider): prevent out of memory errors from tick marks on…
Issues.Body:
The slider only renders its tick marks once it has a width, but it was computing them regardless, allocating one array entry per tick mark. Since the number of entries is derived from the `min`, `max`, `step` and value, a large range or a small step could result in an array big enough to exhaust the heap. This was especially problematic during server-side rendering, because the slider never has a width on the server so the array was always built and then discarded. If any of those inputs are derived from user input (e.g. query parameters), a single request could crash the server process along with every other request it was handling.

These changes skip computing the tick marks until the slider has a width.

Fixes #34036

Issues.Title: bug(MatSlider): showTickMarks can exhaust memory during SSR
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`ngAfterViewInit()` measures the slider only in the browser, but it builds the tick marks on the server too:

```ts
if (this._platform.isBrowser) {
  this._updateDimensions();
}
// ...
this._updateTickMarkUI();
```

`_updateTickMarkUINonRange()` allocates one entry per tick mark:

```ts
this._tickMarks = Array(numActive)
  .fill(_MatTickMark.ACTIVE)
  .concat(Array(numInactive).fill(_MatTickMark.INACTIVE));
```

The template only renders them `@if (_cachedWidth)`, and the server never sets `_cachedWidth`. So during SSR the array is built and thrown away, and nothing bounds its size: it is `(max - min) / step`.

A slider whose bounds come from the URL is enough:

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'price-range',
  imports: [MatSliderModule],
  template: `
    <mat-slider [min]="min" [max]="max" [step]="step" showTickMarks>
      <input matSliderThumb />
    </mat-slider>
  `,
})
export class PriceRange {
  private readonly params = inject(ActivatedRoute).snapshot.queryParamMap;
  readonly min = Number(this.params.get('min') ?? '0');
  readonly max = Number(this.params.get('max') ?? '100');
  readonly step = Number(this.params.get('step') ?? '1');
}
```

I served it with `RenderMode.Server` and compared `/?max=1e9` with a control of the same size, `/?max=1e2`. Each cell is three fresh workers, and `fatal` means a V8 `FATAL ERROR` with exit code 134:

| Heap                | `?max=1e2` | `?max=1e9`           |
| ------------------- | ---------- | -------------------- |
| 256 MiB             | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 3.0 s |
| 1 GiB               | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.5 s |
| 4 GiB               | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.8 s |
| 16 GiB              | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.6 s |
| default (4,288 MiB) | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.6 s |

A bigger heap doesn't help. Above 2^25 entries `Array(n)` switches to dictionary elements, and from about 2.5e8 entries the dictionary hits V8's hash table limit before the heap fills up:

```text
FATAL ERROR: invalid table size Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

`?min=-1e9` and `?step=1e-7` also reach a billion tick marks and are fatal too. The values don't need to look odd either: `?max=1000000&step=0.01`, a price with cents, is 1e8 tick marks and kills a 512 MiB worker.

#26322 fixed #26317 by skipping the array when `showTickMarks` is off. With it on, the count is still unbounded, and #29496 is the browser side of the same problem. #33242 rewrites the method as a `push` loop over `Math.floor((max - min) / step) + 1`, so the count doesn't change. I applied it on top of 22.2.5: `?max=1e9` still kills a 256 MiB worker, `?max=3e7` now does too, and `?step=1e-309` goes from an immediate `RangeError` to a fatal error.

Returning early from `_updateTickMarkUI()` until `_cachedWidth` is set, which the template already requires, makes every request above return 200. The browser still builds the full array once the slider has a width.


As a note I found this while adapting `MatSlider` for a design system, using its code as the base. In an e-commerce app, passing the price filter's value or range through query parameters could OOM the SSR worker, so I would think this is a normal real use case.


### Reproduction

See  https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-material-slider-ssr-oom

Steps to reproduce:

1. `npm ci && npm run build`
2. `npm run serve:ssr:srr-material-oom`
3. `curl "http://localhost:4000/?max=1e9"`


### Expected Behavior

The server renders the slider without building tick marks it can't render, and the worker keeps serving other requests.


### Actual Behavior

The SSR worker aborts with a V8 fatal error (exit code 134), and every request in flight on it fails with it.


### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4, `@angular/ssr` 22.2.5, Node.js 24.16.0 (also 21.2.25 and 20.3.34)
- CDK/Material: 22.2.5 (also 21.2.14 and 20.2.14). `main` and 22.3.0-next.4 have the same code.
- Browser(s): n/a, server-side rendering
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Windows 11 x64

Issues.Title: feat(cdk Portal): Allow DomPortal to reference detached elements
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

There is a built-in security that blocks a detached element (one that has no parent node) to be used in a DomPortal, [here](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/265b8a48718fda931ef6c57b30b371fcd926707b/src/cdk/portal/dom-portal-outlet.ts#L145).
The only purpose of this bit of code is to ensure that _if_ the DOM node is obtained the nominal way, i.e from the component's view, then it gets put back where it was before, when the operation is done or it stops being used.

### Use Case

I have a dependency that generates DOM nodes (SVG nodes to be precise). I was using a custom directive that was using `inject(ElementRef).nativeElement` and `.replaceChildren(this.inputDOMNode())`, which works but is not great.

I discovered Portal and thought I could use it, but I actually can't because the built-in security prevents me from passing a detached element to DOMPortal(). I guess I could instanciate a dummy DOM node (itself detached) to attach all my SVG nodes to it before passing them to the DOMPortal, but that's nonsense really, I just don't need the housekeeping feature of placing the node back where it was found.

Issues.Title: feat(Paginator): Fix the default "1 – 10 of 100" syntax
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

By default, [Paginator](https://material.angular.dev/components/paginator/overview) shows text like "1 – 10 of 100". The space around the en-dash is incorrect syntax. There is no style guide that uses that. Even British style guides, e.g., [New Hart's Rules: The Oxford Style Guide](https://oceanide.es/losarchivos/docs/new-harts-rules-2005.pdf), which use spaces around en-dashes in some situations, don't use it for ranges.

The correct text should be "1–10 of 100".

### Use Case

While this can be replaced through `MatPaginatorIntl`, the default English label should also be correct for projects that do not need i18n. I know this is a "breaking change" as it might break screenshot and text-based tests, but it can be done for a major release.

Issues.Title: bug(material/datepicker): Focus moves to a date cell instead of returning to the period button after selecting a year/month (WCAG 2.4.3)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No, this behaviour has always existed.

### Description

When the calendar’s period button (“Choose month and year”) is activated by keyboard, the calendar switches to the multi-year view and then the year view. After the user selects a year and then a month, the calendar returns to the month view and focus moves to a date cell in the calendar grid. It does not return to the period button that opened the view.

This affects keyboard and screen reader users. They can’t easily change the month or year again, because the next Tab or Shift+Tab stop is unpredictable. They have to navigate back through the grid to reach the period button. We believe this fails WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order) in accessibility audits, because the focus destination after the interaction doesn’t preserve a logical, predictable order relative to the control that triggered it.

### Reproduction

This reproduces on the official Angular Material documentation example: https://material.angular.dev/components/datepicker/overview#datepicker-custom-icon

Steps to reproduce (keyboard only):
1.Open the datepicker with the “Open calendar” button (Enter).
2.Press Tab until the “Choose month and year” period button is focused, then press Enter.
3.Use the arrow keys to select a year and press Enter.
4.Use the arrow keys to select a month and press Enter.
5.Observe where focus lands.


### Expected Behavior

Focus returns to the period button that opened the view, so users can change the month/year again or Tab onward predictably. Alternatively, expose an option to control this, for example an input on mat-calendar.

### Actual Behavior

Focus moves to a date cell (.mat-calendar-body-cell) in the month grid. The period button loses focus and the user has to navigate back to it manually.

### Environment

- Angular: 19.2.14
- CDK/Material: 19.2.19
- Browser(s): Chrome, Safari
- Operating System : macOS

Issues.Title: bug(aria/accordion): Enter/Space inside a panel toggles the accordion instead of activating the focused element
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Enter on a link (or Space on a button) inside an expanded `ngAccordionPanel` collapses the panel instead of activating the link/button.

`ngAccordionGroup` handles `keydown` for the whole group, including panel content, and calls `preventDefault()` on Enter/Space, so the focused element never gets activated. Arrow keys and Home/End are affected too, e.g. Home in an input inside a panel moves focus to the trigger.

The click handler only reacts to events coming from a trigger (`_findTriggerPattern`), the keydown handler doesn't check that:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/952685f9370ba718f832d745512db7c9a04e1bcd/src/aria/private/accordion/accordion.ts#L73-L97

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/z5sxyaq6?file=src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Expand "Section 1".
2. Tab to "Link inside panel" or "Button inside panel" and press Enter / Space.
3. Expand it again, click into the input and press Home.

### Expected Behavior

The link/button is activated (shows up in the log) and the panel stays open. Home moves the caret in the input.

### Actual Behavior

The panel collapses, nothing is activated. Home moves focus to the trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: @angular/aria 22.2.4 (also 22.1.6)
- Browser(s): Chrome 155
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Linux
